claims.text: app-web (Caddy on :8081) answers a path that is not a real file, such as /products/3, with the app's index.html via try_files {path} /index.html; the app starts and its router reads the path from the address bar to pick the screen.
claims.source_hint: deploy/app-web/Caddyfile @ stage-4 lines 10-14; Caddy docs: try_files directive

claims.text: The <body> of DonHang.App's index.html at stage-4 holds only the comment Flutter wrote when the project was created and <script src="flutter_bootstrap.js" async></script>: no product name, no price.

what-the-server-sends.sh reads product 3's name from GET :8080/api/v1/products/3 (Tai nghe), fetches /products/3 from app-web :8081, prints its <body> and reports 'product name in the HTML: no'; then prints the text of www/index.html on :8080.

In the browser, flutter_bootstrap.js starts the app: the browser downloads Flutter's engine and main.dart.js (the app compiled to JavaScript), the app runs, and the product screen requests /api/v1/products/3 from :8080, which proxies to the API; the name is drawn only after that JSON arrives.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: platform-integration/web/initialization (flutter_bootstrap.js); ADR 0017 @ stage-4 lines 48-50; frontend.l2.deep-links (productProvider)

claims.text: Server-side rendering: the server builds, per request, HTML that already contains the page's text, readable without running code.
www/index.html served on :8080 is a hand-written page whose text (Đơn Hàng, Trang tĩnh của phòng lab stage-0., three link labels) is in the HTML file itself.

Flutter web FAQ (SEO): Flutter web output doesn't align with what search engines need to index (record a page's words so people find it by them); for static, document-like content HTML is one recommended option, apart from the Flutter app. A reader taking only this HTML records no product name.
claims.source_hint: Flutter docs: platform-integration/web/faq.md, section 'Search Engine Optimization (SEO)' (refs/flutter-website)

claims.text: ADR 0017 consequence: HTML app-web returns for a product page lacks the product name (what-the-server-sends.sh); public product pages for search, if needed, are server-built HTML apart from the app, decided in a separate ADR; ordering stays in the app.
The browser's page source view shows the HTML the server sent for the address, not what the app drew afterwards.
claims.source_hint: frontend.l1.html-css-js-roles Try it (page source); browser documentation for view-source

claims.text: Trade-offs: the app's page costs nothing until search matters; hand-written files suit text that rarely changes, not a changing catalogue for 1,000 shops; server-built pages give every reader the name at the price of a second piece of software that shows products.

Choices: if customers arrive only by links from the shop, keep the app page; if many shops need indexable product pages, write the separate ADR and weigh server-built pages linking to the app's deep link; static help text fits a hand-written HTML page.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0017 lines 51-55; Flutter web FAQ (SEO); frontend.l2.deep-links

claims.text: Every reader first gets the same index.html; the name shows only because the browser runs the app; ADR 0017 splits ordering (app) from public pages (server-built HTML); Flutter's docs suggest a similar split for landing, marketing and help content; search alone does not justify a rewrite.
claims.source_hint: Misconceptions 1-3; ADR 0017 lines 51-55; Flutter web FAQ (SEO)
